properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 9 at 1:34PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9
to 14 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of near 7.0 ft (MLLW) are
expected each morning. The High Surf and Coastal Flood
Advisories may need to be extended through the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL NOON PST TUESDAY... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL NOON PST TUESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Malibu Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 1:34PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding during
morning high tides, as well as dangerous rip currents and
breaking waves due to elevated surf up to 4 to 6 feet
expected, especially across west facing beaches.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands and Malibu Coast.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak on
Monday. Since the large swell is from the west, south facing
areas such as Malibu be less affected unlike the previous
events where the swell was from the south.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9
to 14 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of near 7.0 ft (MLLW) are
expected each morning. The High Surf and Coastal Flood
Advisories may need to be extended through the week.

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Weather Service when you can do so safely.

night.

likely. This will lead to whiteout conditions, making travel

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 12:13PM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04
AM Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.4 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

into early this week, leading to a rise in river levels that may
approach action stage late tonight.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground

- At 12:15 PM CST Monday the stage was 2.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 5.9 feet
early Wednesday afternoon.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 130 AM CST.

the Ventura Harbor entrance into the evening. These conditions
have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in
serious injury or death, even to the most experienced mariners.

information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard
station, and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest
weather information..

including the low water crossing of Ranch Road 3404/Slab Road near

loosened downstream in Kingsland.

- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage just after
midnight tonight to 11.3 feet late tonight. It will then fall
late tomorrow morning. It will rise to 10.9 feet early tomorrow
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 9 at 9:57AM AST until November 10 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering northerly swells generated by
distant surface low over the central Atlantic will support
breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet and a high risk of life-
threatening rip currents along the northern exposed beaches of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH TUESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 9 at 5:06AM PST until November 10 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding expected.
Additionally, dangerous rip currents and surf of 3 to 7 feet
expected along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of parking lots and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming conditions
due to elevated surf and strong rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest tides will occur in the morning
each day, peaking at 7.2-7.4 feet today, which is 1.2 to 1.4
feet above astronomical tide predictions. Higher surf today
could prolong coastal impacts.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water to avoid
hazardous swimming conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
